Jeff Wadlin

Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate, Arkansas · Challenger

Strategy consultant / business owner (Bentonville)

Jeff Wadlin is a businessman from Bentonville who owns a consulting business and has worked at Caterpillar, Capital One and Sam's Club. He won the Libertarian Party convention nomination unopposed on February 22, 2026, and launched his general election campaign on May 19, 2026. He calls himself an independent and a centrist, and says he ran on the Libertarian ticket because it qualified him for the ballot automatically, without the signature-gathering that unaffiliated candidates must do.

Where Wadlin stands

Cost of living / economy
Says Arkansas's middle class is being squeezed. Supports policies to lower costs, raise wages and 'build ladders into the middle class' through practical reforms rather than what he calls permanent dependence.
Debates
Took part in the Oct. 12 Arkansas TV debate and criticized Sen. Cotton for not attending. Says Cotton agreed to debate Shoffner but not him, and that he was left out of the Salem Media debate offer.
Partisanship / governing approach
Calls himself a centrist and 'Arkansas-first independent.' Argues that both major parties put culture-war fights ahead of economic interests and 'somehow' work together to produce bad outcomes.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate, Arkansas (convention, Feb. 22, 2026); no prior elected office found
  • Owner of a consulting business; previously worked at Caterpillar, Capital One and Sam's Club
  • B.S., mechanical engineering, University of Virginia (also studied aerospace engineering)
  • MBA, Northwestern University
  • Born in Richmond, Virginia; lives in Bentonville, Arkansas
